summary: The pure-Python NeuroSem stack was installed and tested on Windows 11 from exact PyPI pins: pyNeuroML 1.3.22, libNeuroML 0.6.7, PyLEMS 0.6.9, neuromllite 0.6.1, efel 5.7.34, OSBModelValidation 0.4.0 and pytest 9.1.1. The pip resolver chose numpy 2.5.3, scipy 1.18.1, lxml 6.1.3, tables 3.11.1 and matplotlib 3.11.2. Tests were run in venvs under the scratch folder. On Python 3.12.10: pip install worked, pip check was clean, all imports worked, and the bundled jar reports JNEUROML_VERSION 0.14.0 with sha256 45ee565a...db931. A NeuroML2 example (NML2_SingleCompHHCell.nml from NeuroML/NeuroML2 at commit a5f5dad; LGPL-3.0 repo) passed XSD validation with lxml against libNeuroML's bundled NeuroML_v2.3.1.xsd, and also passed libNeuroML is_valid_neuroml2. A negative control with conductance='10mA' was rejected by both. The same install, imports and validation also worked on Python 3.14.7. Dependencies were locked with 'uv pip compile --universal --python-version 3.12 --generate-hashes' (uv 0.12.13): 73 packages, 1393 sha256 hashes. A fresh venv then installed with 'pip install --require-hashes --no-deps', and pip check and imports passed. Java-backed steps fail as expected because Java is absent: 'pynml <file> -validate' exits 1. Recommended Java is Eclipse Temurin 21 JRE (LTS, supported to at least Dec 2029 per Adoptium). It is the newest LTS inside jNeuroML 0.14.0's CI matrix (Java 8-21); Temurin 25 is also LTS but untested by jNeuroML CI. The winget ID EclipseAdoptium.Temurin.21.JRE was verified from the winget-pkgs manifest: machine-scope WiX MSI, needs admin. A per-user ZIP alternative is given. Linux CI, the Dockerfile, the Java install, jnml validation and jLEMS simulation are proposed but NOT tested.

java_install.notes: Verified facts: (1) The Adoptium API (https://api.adoptium.net/v3/info/available_releases) lists LTS releases 8, 11, 17, 21 and 25; most_recent_lts 25; most_recent_feature_release 26. (2) The Adoptium support roadmap (https://adoptium.net/support/, read through the WebFetch summariser) gives these minimum support dates: 8 at least Dec 2030; 11 and 17 at least Oct 2027; 21 at least Dec 2029; 25 at least Sep 2031; 26 non-LTS to Sep 2026. (3) winget manifests: PackageIdentifier EclipseAdoptium.Temurin.21.JRE, versions 21.0.12.8 and 21.0.12.101 present. InstallerType wix, Scope machine, InstallerUrl github.com/adoptium/temurin21-binaries .../OpenJDK21U-jre_x64_windows_hotspot_21.0.12.1_1.msi, License 'GPL-2.0 with Classpath Exception'. EclipseAdoptium.Temurin.25.JRE 25.0.4.101 also exists. The Adoptium installation page shows the pattern 'winget install EclipseAdoptium.Temurin.25.JDK' (https://adoptium.net/installation/). (4) Adoptium Windows MSI docs (https://adoptium.net/installation/windows/): features FeatureMain, FeatureEnvironment (PATH), FeatureJarFileRunWith and FeatureJavaHome (JAVA_HOME, not default with INSTALLLEVEL=1). The installer is per-machine, not per-user. Example: msiexec /i <package>.msi ADDLOCAL=FeatureMain,FeatureEnvironment,FeatureJarFileRunWith,FeatureJavaHome INSTALLDIR="c:\Program Files\Temurin\" /quiet. (5) What jNeuroML needs (from verified tool facts, not re-fetched): jNeuroML 0.14.0 is compiled with source/target 1.8, and its CI workflow at v0.14.0 builds from source on Temurin Java 8, 11, 16, 17, 19 and 21. The docs state no explicit minimum. The pyNeuroML README lists only 'Java Runtime environment (JRE)' and an apt 'openjdk-11-jdk' example (re-checked at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeuroML/pyNeuroML/v1.3.22/README.md lines 31 and 38). Choosing 21 over 25 is a judgment call: 21 is the newest LTS inside jNeuroML's CI range. Java 25 with the bundled jar is untested anywhere this audit could find. (6) A JRE is enough to run the jar; a JDK is not needed. Do NOT install during M0. Installing needs Neel's approval, and he must run the machine-scope MSI himself.

dockerfile_sketch:
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
# NOT TESTED (no Docker on the audit machine). Tags verified on Docker Hub 2026-09-13.
# Pin by digest in M1: the amd64 image digest seen for python:3.12.14-slim-trixie was
# sha256:2fe5997d249a808b8eeea52c58a1dbffbba28754dc11699ef5c029f2d818ce79 (per-arch digest, not the multi-arch index digest).
FROM python:3.12.14-slim-trixie

# Java runtime: Debian trixie package openjdk-21-jre-headless (21.0.12.1+1-1~deb13u1 per packages.debian.org).
# Alternative for exact Temurin parity with CI/Windows (untested glibc mix):
#   COPY --from=eclipse-temurin:21.0.12_8-jre-noble /opt/java/openjdk /opt/java/openjdk
#   ENV JAVA_HOME=/opt/java/openjdk PATH=/opt/java/openjdk/bin:$PATH
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends openjdk-21-jre-headless \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1 \
    JNML_MAX_MEMORY_LOCAL=2G
# (JNML_MAX_MEMORY_LOCAL must be set before pyneuroml is imported)

WORKDIR /opt/neurosem
COPY requirements.lock.txt ./
RUN python -m pip install pip==26.2.1 \
 && python -m pip install --require-hashes --no-deps -r requirements.lock.txt \
 && python -m pip check

COPY pyproject.toml README.md ./
COPY src ./src
RUN python -m pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation -e .
# (editable install without build isolation needs the build backend in the lock; otherwise use a normal wheel build step)

# Provenance: fail the build if the bundled jNeuroML jar changes
RUN java -version \
 && python -c "import hashlib; from pyneuroml.utils.misc import get_path_to_jnml_jar as g; h=hashlib.sha256(open(g(),'rb').read()).hexdigest(); assert h=='45ee565a65a66008a3b41935358d11b7c19cb6b5a67bbec22481d519f53db931', h"

COPY tests ./tests
CMD ["pytest", "-q", "tests"]

dependency_freezing.recommended: uv 0.12.13 'uv pip compile requirements.in --universal --python-version 3.12 --generate-hashes -o requirements.lock.txt', installed with 'pip install --require-hashes --no-deps -r requirements.lock.txt' (both tested OK on Windows). Keep requirements.in (top-level exact pins) and requirements.lock.txt in git, and record the lock file's sha256 in every run manifest.
alternatives: pip-tools 7.6.1: 'pip-compile --generate-hashes requirements.in' then 'pip-sync' (README https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jazzband/pip-tools/main/README.md; 'pip-compile --help' in 7.6.1 lists --generate-hashes). Installed and version confirmed; compile not run. Unlike uv --universal, its output is resolved for the current platform/interpreter.

uv project lock: 'uv lock' writes uv.lock; 'uv sync --locked' asserts uv.lock will remain unchanged; 'uv sync --frozen' syncs without updating it; 'uv lock --check' checks it is up to date (from local 'uv --help' output of 0.12.13). Needs a pyproject.toml project; not tested.
'pip freeze --all' snapshot (81 lines captured in logs/pip_freeze_312.txt) as a human-readable environment digest only; it has no hashes and is platform-specific.
dependency_freezing.environment_yml_note: The handoff repository tree lists environment.yml (a conda file), but conda is not installed and the zero-budget/no-conda constraint applies. Replace it with requirements.in + requirements.lock.txt (or uv.lock) plus the Dockerfile. This is a decision for Neel.

blockers: No Java runtime on the Windows machine, and installing one was not permitted in M0. jnml validation, jLEMS simulation, OMV jNeuroML engines and the M1 exit test ('one command validates and simulates both models') cannot run until Neel approves and installs Temurin 21 (winget MSI is machine-scope and needs admin; ZIP per-user route available).
No Docker on the machine, so the Dockerfile cannot be built or tested locally; it must be built in GitHub Actions or on another host (decision needed).

Windows-specific jNeuroML/pyNeuroML risks from the tool audit remain: the -I include path is split on ':' (breaks drive-letter paths); stderr is not captured on Windows, so a missing Java looks like an invalid model; OMV needs HOME, PATH and UTF-8 workarounds. Recommendation: treat Linux (CI/Docker) as the reference platform for frozen runs and keep Windows for development and Java-free checks.

Study fixtures are not selected here. The NML2_SingleCompHHCell.nml file used is only a validation smoke test from the LGPL-3.0 NeuroML2 repository; fixture choice and license belong to the fixture audit and need Neel's approval.

Python 3.12 vs 3.14: three core packages (libNeuroML, neuromllite, OSBModelValidation) do not claim 3.14 support, and networkx 3.6.1 excludes CPython 3.14.1; the frozen interpreter must be decided (3.12 recommended).
